Hi Priya — great to hear. Short answer: yes, we can support reverse-charge flow for registered B2B sellers and avoid GST withholding when a validated GSTIN is present. Below is a proposed mutual action plan and the documents we need from each seller.

Mutual action plan (draft) — timeline target: 2 weeks to enable pilot:
- Day 0: ShopVista provides sample invoices + GSTIN list for initial 50 sellers (you provided sample invoice — thanks).
- Day 2: Redwood tax team reviews sample and confirms invoice wording + required metadata (invoice line item for reverse-charge, seller tax ID, buyer tax ID).
- Day 4: Redwood provides RC invoice template (attached) + validation rules and API spec for GSTIN validation.
- Day 7: ShopVista implements API calls / portal upload for seller GSTINs; Redwood validates via tax-registry checks & flags exempt sellers.
- Day 10-14: End-to-end test with 5 seller invoices; if green, enable pilot.

Required merchant docs for exemption (per seller):
- GSTIN registration certificate (scanned PDF)
- Official business name that matches GST registry
- Billing contact + email

Notes on system behavior:
- If GSTIN validated -> mark seller as exempt and do not apply GST withholding; invoice will include a standard reverse-charge statement (we'll provide exact language).
- If GSTIN fails validation -> system will default to withholding path and flag for manual review.

Attaching: redwood_rc-invoice-template.xlsx and a short integration manifest example (shopvista_integration_manifest.json) for the onboarding payload.

Can we schedule a 30-minute call with your integration lead tomorrow to review the API spec? I can loop in Ben (billing) and Markus (tax).

Best,

Thanks for the ping — I can own the billing changes. Quick notes:
- We already support a per-seller tax exemption flag in Billing v2; it's toggled via the merchant onboarding API.
- Need to confirm the validation source: India GST registry lookups are rate-limited and occasionally return partial matches. We should implement a 2-step approach: (1) automated registry lookup (primary), (2) manual document upload + audit trail (fallback).
- Invoice template: we'll adopt your RC line; need to confirm whether ShopVista wants the buyer or seller to carry the reverse-charge wording. For marketplaces, the marketplace (ShopVista) is typically the buyer of the platform fee and should be the entity referenced on platform invoices.

Technical asks for integration:
- API endpoint to POST seller records: seller_id, business_name, gstin, contact_email, proof_url. (manifest attached by Jordan).
- Response codes: 200 (validated), 202 (queued/manual review), 422 (invalid format).
- Webhook for status updates back to ShopVista on validation outcome.

Risk/control: if GSTIN fails validation and the invoice gateway marks a transaction as non-exempt, we need to trigger a collection hold and notify finance. That would be a manual release only.

I'll draft the billing API spec and the UI flag story. Expect a first pass by EOD today.

-ben

Jordan/Ben — tax perspective below. High level: reverse-charge treatment is acceptable for B2B sellers with validated GSTINs. A few specifics to include in the implementation: 

1) Validation sources: rely on the GST portal / registry. Persist a snapshot of the registry response (GSTIN, legal name, validation timestamp) in our audit logs for each seller. That snapshot is the evidence we will retain for audits.
2) Invoice wording (recommended): 
   "Supply subject to reverse charge as per Section 9(3) of the CGST Act" (or local equivalent). Also include: "Recipient liable to pay GST under reverse charge" and list the buyer GSTIN (ShopVista).
3) Evidence retention: store the merchant-supplied PDF and the registry snapshot, tie both to the seller record and invoice. Retention policy: 7 years for APAC (per local guidance).
4) Edge cases: for sellers with recently updated registrations (name mismatch), flag for manual tax team review. Do not auto-exempt until manual sign-off.
5) Reporting: include a daily summary for finance that lists newly exempted sellers and any suspended invoices.

If Ben can provide the API hook and data model, tax will sign off on the template. We'll supply the exact invoice text and the minimum audit fields required.

-Markus
